name: Template — auth (log on / register / OTP)
$fence: EXAMPLE, NOT A PART. Dave, 14:55 2026-10-02, call 7, verbatim: "the page templates are only example or inspiration in the library for designers. automated build need to ignore these, I don't want builds to trace pages. However we probably need to create some standardised templates for some programs. They all need to be properly built. for now we have the prepped properly but we ignore them until we are working with programs to define them." So: this page is properly composed of parts (s313-D72) AND fenced — the compose door (_compose_slice.py load_graph) skips it, the generate-from-canon skill never starts from it, and _validate_example_fence.py refuses a build that reads or traces it.
purpose: The unauthenticated entry pages: log on, register, and one-time passcode. A quiet brand column beside a single narrow form column, collapsing to one column. It contributes page-scale layout and the brand placement; every control inside it is a gated component, borrowed.
$provenance-note: NEW at #210 (wave 5, lane C) against the Layer-2 P2 fan-out brief - itinerary row 112. PROPOSED, NOT RULED. No registration was performed: no CATEGORIES entry, no MIGRATED_SNIPPETS entry, no component-types.json membership, no canon.css block, no _rulings.json line, no git operation.
$layer-note: The brief PROPOSED the meta key `layer`. meta.schema.json is additionalProperties:false with patternProperties '^\\$' only, so a bare `layer` key FAILS probe P-1 (probe_meta_schema.py). `$layer` is the legal form.
$specimen-fence: ⛔ THIS TEMPLATE AUTHENTICATES NOTHING AND MUST NEVER BE READ AS A SECURITY DESIGN. No credential is checked, no OTP is verified, no session is created, no value is stored or transmitted, there is no network call of any kind. Every consequential handler writes to an aria-live region and returns. The only client-side logic is FORMAT validation borrowed from Form-layout (is the field empty; does the string contain an @; is it 12 characters) - never an identity or secret check. No copy in the file asserts encryption, protection, monitoring or any other security property; where a real product puts an assurance line, this file deliberately puts nothing.

$composes-note: REBUILT #314 lane TP (s313-D72, Dave's comment verbatim: "We need to regenerate the templates too BTW, everything in the library should be a valid 'element' of the design system"). The template is a composed PAGE: its snippet links canon/canon.css and places each part above as its own .cn-<slug> scope with the part's own markup; the page's <style> carries placement rules only (s305-D57 rule 3a; s307-D75). Before #314 it carried copies of the parts' rules and canon.css projected that second copy under its own scope. The #210 prose that stood here (which classes were copied, declaration for declaration) is retired with the copies. FIX ROUND #314 TP: the password reveal is a quaternary Button under the box, words only (s313-D49), with three lines of page wiring; the OTP Continue carries Button's own is-disabled state; the lede is page prose under the lock-up.

accessibility.roles: No invented roles. The error box is role=alert with tabindex=-1; the OTP cells are a role=group named by their label; the OTP message is role=status.
accessibility.keyboard: Every control is a real focusable element. The reveal toggle returns focus to its field so typing continues uninterrupted. OTP cells auto-advance on input and step back on backspace from an empty cell.
accessibility.announcements: Per-field aria-live=polite messages; a visually-hidden live region per panel carries the placeholder outcomes so a screen-reader user learns that the specimen did nothing rather than being left in silence.
accessibility.states: aria-invalid per field; aria-pressed on the reveal toggle; the Continue button's disabled state tracks code completeness only.
accessibility.targets: Every primary/secondary button is 44px tall and full width. The reveal toggle and every inline text link have a REAL 44px box, not an invisible expander (the #210 wizard lesson).
accessibility.autocomplete: 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose, checked in a real browser: username, current-password, name, email, new-password, one-time-code. Every credential field also carries autocapitalize=none, autocorrect=off and spellcheck=false so a password manager and a soft keyboard both behave.
accessibility.$noVisibilityGlyph: ⚠ MEASURED ON THE #210 BUILD, before the #314 rebuild as a composed page; not re-measured at #314. MEASURED GAP, not an omission. Probe run at build: `ls knowledge/assets/icons/*/ | grep -iE "eye|visib|hide|show|reveal|password"` returns masthead-hide.svg and masthead-show.svg (arrows-and-rules - a MASTHEAD collapse control) and security-password.svg (a keyboard-with-dots). None of them means 'reveal what I typed'. The reveal control is therefore a TEXT toggle, which needs no glyph and announces its own state. An _ICON-GAPS.md entry may be owed; that file is the conductor's (the #209 Q14 precedent).
accessibility.$noPasswordField: Input-fields.reference.html contains no type="password" field of any kind - the only masked inputs in the whole snippet corpus are Secure-entry's PIN cells. The password field here is the gated boxed-field anatomy with type="password": composed, not drawn, and PROPOSED.
accessibility.$colourIsNeverAlone: The error channel is border + 4px stroke + roundel + ink message text. The password requirements are plain ink list items, not a live tick/cross meter - a meter would need a RAG vocabulary this lane has no mandate to mint.

antiPatterns: ⛔ Placing the Apollo crescent, or any drawn approximation of the HSBC mark, on an auth screen. Reference the official asset file or show no mark at all.
⛔ Adding real credential or OTP logic to this specimen, or copying it into anything that authenticates. It exists to show layout and states.
⛔ Writing security assurance copy ('your data is protected', 'we monitor every log on'). This template deliberately makes no security claim; a claim in a design specimen becomes a claim in a product.
Inventing an eye icon for the reveal toggle because the library has none. Use words.
Omitting or guessing autocomplete. A wrong autocomplete token is worse than none: it teaches a password manager to fill the wrong field.
Telling a person which of username or password was wrong. This specimen's messages are format messages ('Enter your username'), never outcome messages.
REVIEW Filling the brand column with invented imagery. It is deliberately quiet: the mark and one neutral line. Brand imagery is not this lane's to create.

Copying a part's rules onto the page. The page places parts (its own .cn-<slug> scope + the part's own markup) and never resizes or restyles them (s305-D57 rule 3a, s307-D75). A template that re-declares a Button ladder, a Summary row or a Data-grid toolbar forks the part the moment the part moves.

$brandMark.$fence: Dave #86: the Apollo crescent is an ANONYMITY mark ONLY and must NEVER be placed as a product brand. This template contains no crescent and creates no brand asset.
$brandMark.$provenance: Exported from the Foundations > Logos Figma page by knowledge/assets/logos/_export-logos.py. Referenced as FILES via ; no logo path data is inlined anywhere and no recolouring is applied.
$brandMark.$idiom: FIRST src-BEARING IN ANY GATED SNIPPET, and the probe form is load-bearing: `grep -l '` inside its header COMMENT. The true probe is `grep -l ']*src=' knowledge/snippets/*.reference.html`, which returns this file alone (6 hits here, 0 in Image-block). Inlining the logo was REJECTED on a measurement: _validate_icons.py byte-matches inline paths against assets/icons/ ONLY, and the logos live in assets/logos/, so an inlined mark would land as UNKNOWN - indistinguishable from an invented one. Whether the library ADOPTS the idiom is the conductor's / Dave's call, not this lane's.
$brandMark.$rendered: Both files were LOADED in a real browser and measured: naturalWidth>0 for all six elements, exactly one visible per theme, 160x43 CSS px, alt="HSBC", zero failed requests.
$brandMark.$schema-note: Homed under a $-prefixed key because meta.schema.json is additionalProperties:false with patternProperties '^\\$' only. A bare `brandMark` key FAILED probe P-1 at first write ("'brandMark' does not match any of the regexes: '^\\$'") and this is the correction, recorded not hidden. Same class as the brief's proposed `layer` key.
